rules.statement: A workflow that publishes NuGet packages must authenticate through nuget.org trusted publishing (`NuGet/login` exchanging the job's OIDC token for a job-lived key), never through a long-lived API key stored in a secret.
rules.why: Trusted publishing issues a key that lives only for the job and is scoped to the repository, workflow and environment, so no long-lived key exists to leak.
rules.check: Look in publish workflows for `dotnet nuget push --api-key ${{ secrets.* }}` or any NuGet API key secret, instead of a `NuGet/login` step with `id-token: write`.

rules.statement: Split package publishing into a read-only build job that runs the build, tests and packing and uploads the packages, and a separate publish job that runs in a protected deployment environment with only `contents: read` and `id-token: write`.
rules.why: Write-scoped or token-minting permissions must stay out of the job that runs third-party build and test code, and the environment records the required reviewers' approval against the deployment.
rules.check: Check that the job running `dotnet build`/`test`/`pack` has no write or `id-token` permission, and that the push job declares an `environment:` and grants no permissions beyond `contents: read` and `id-token: write`.

rules.statement: Trigger package publishing only deliberately, from a version tag or a manual run on a protected branch, never on every push or merge to the trunk.
rules.why: nuget.org versions are permanent, and a version per merge buries the ones a deployment needs.
rules.check: Look for a publish workflow with an `on: push: branches: [main]` trigger, or any trigger other than version tags and `workflow_dispatch`.

rules.statement: A tag-triggered publish workflow must verify that the tagged commit is already held by the trunk or a release line, and that the tag names exactly the version the packages were packed with, before publishing.
rules.why: A tag on an unreviewed commit must publish nothing, and the published version must be the one the tag names.
rules.check: In a tag-triggered publish workflow, look for the absence of a check that the tag's commit is an ancestor of `main` or a `release/v*` branch, or of a check comparing the tag to the packed package version.

rules.statement: A NuGet publish step must fail when every package of the version is already on nuget.org, push with `--skip-duplicate` so a partially failed run completes when rerun, and push each package's `.snupkg` to the symbol server.
rules.why: A run on an unchanged version must fail instead of reporting success for nothing, while a rerun after a partial failure must still complete.
rules.check: Check the push step for `--skip-duplicate`, symbol package pushes, and a preceding check that refuses an already fully published version.

rules.statement: Don't put a `{height}` or other commit-height suffix in the prerelease version in `version.json`; a prerelease name is set explicitly by bumping the version.
rules.why: A prerelease name is a decision, not a counter, and a tag must be able to name the version before the commit exists.
rules.check: Look for `{height}` in the `version` field of `version.json`.

rules.statement: Gate promotion to a hosted environment through a GitHub deployment environment with its own required reviewers and secrets, not through which branch the workflow runs on.
rules.why: A branch records no approval for a deployment; an environment records the approval against the deployment.
rules.check: Look for deploy jobs that rely only on a branch condition (`if: github.ref == ...`) and declare no `environment:`, or that read deployment secrets from repository-level secrets.
